# Veilo

> Veilo is an owner-controlled AI agent workspace with delegated spending controls and a shared private funding pool on Solana devnet.

Status: the recorded M2 pool/PayAI Echo run is verified on devnet. Integrated flows are verified on local test validator with a fixture / mock provider. A parallel branch records a later devnet gateway execution, but complete task/live-inference acceptance evidence is missing here. Marketplace acceptance is not yet run in this checkout. The deterministic development setup has derivable toxic waste and is for test funds only.

PRD v3.2 accepts a marketplace of reviewed paid specialists: searchable listings, seller review, private jobs/deliverables, direct seller x402 settlement, zero platform fee and receipt-based earnings. Supabase holds marketplace identity/product records; local control/wallet retain spending authority. Cloud sign-in cannot authorize money, and the local P0 stack still works without Supabase. These marketplace capabilities are pending, not shipped.

Existing execution uses credit-manager, research and content roles; generic templates are a T19 requirement. Owners configure names, jobs, triggers, budgets and approved services. Shawn, Prince and Mira are workflow examples, not a fixed list of agents. The model proposes resources; independent control and wallet services authorize purchases.

The private flow aims to remove the explicit link from a particular deposited note to a payout. Fresh-wallet payments, merchants, amounts and timing remain public. Owners retain local agent attribution; the gateway can link authenticated usage. Do not infer universal anonymity, production readiness, deployed behavior or successful security tests from these documentation pages.

# Specialist-agent marketplace

**Status: accepted scope, implementation pending in this checkout; end-to-end acceptance is not yet run.** PRD v3.2 §26 adds this marketplace to the existing private-wallet workspace. It does not remove the original payment, privacy or recovery requirements. [Marketplace triage](./marketplace-triage.md) records the code gaps and T17–T23 release gates.

## Buy work or offer a specialist

Owners create agents with their own names, instructions, triggers, tools and independently enforced budgets. The marketplace extends those agents with reviewed, fixed-price specialists. A buyer can hire manually, or let an agent discover and propose a specialist. A new seller still needs owner approval before payment. Models propose work; local control authorizes money.

The required first release includes:

| Buyer experience | Seller experience |
|---|---|
| Wallet sign-in and a searchable catalogue of reviewed listings | Self-service seller setup followed by operator review before publication |
| One specialist per hire, with an immutable fixed-price, fixed-scope quote | Direct settlement to the listing's verified seller recipient |
| Private job board, requests for missing inputs, downloadable deliverables and receipts | Assigned-job access and a history of finalized earnings receipts |
| Manual hiring or discovery within owner-approved permissions | Managed templates or reviewed remote endpoints, with read-only connectors by default |

These are requirements, not screens or endpoints available in the current application. The seeded six-SKU gateway catalogue is a local service catalogue; it is not the searchable seller marketplace. Generic templates are also pending: current execution is limited to credit-manager, research and content roles. Shawn, Prince and Mira become templates in T19 rather than defining the marketplace's full agent model.

## Two sign-ins, two responsibilities

The marketplace uses **Supabase Auth, Postgres and Storage** for accounts, catalogue, private jobs, artifact metadata and accounting projections. Each workspace retains one owner; multiple independent buyer/seller accounts do not create a shared multi-owner wallet.

Supabase Web3 sign-in establishes marketplace identity. The existing local wallet challenge establishes spending authority. A connected but unsigned wallet grants no private-data access, and a cloud session never authorizes a withdrawal. Cloud policy edits remain proposals until local control installs and acknowledges them.

Local control connects outbound using authenticated, digest-bound, expiring requests. It retains authority over policies, reservations and revocation; the local wallet retains notes, proofs and signing keys. Automatic spending pauses while local control is offline. The original T00–T16 local workspace must keep working without Supabase. There is no implemented cloud connection or Supabase setup command in this checkout yet.

[Diagram definition included below.]

## Direct seller payments and receipts

For a paid hire, an immutable quote names the reviewed listing and runtime versions, seller payout version, exact recipient, network, mint, amount and expiry. Local control rechecks approval and every applicable allowance. The wallet proves a pool withdrawal to a fresh signer, then validates an ordinary x402 V2 exact payment to that seller. Execution starts only after independently verified finality; an explicitly free quote may start without payment.

The platform fee is explicitly **zero** in each quote and receipt: `F = floor(B × r / 10000)`, with `r = 0`. Seller earnings are a history of settled chain receipts, not a withdrawable platform balance. The platform must not receive seller funds as an intermediate merchant.

The existing client supports approved per-service recipient bindings, but the Veilo gateway currently accepts its single configured merchant. **Managed paid listings remain blocked until per-listing recipients are implemented and verified.** A separately operated compliant seller endpoint is a possible integration path; live third-party seller payment and marketplace hiring have not been demonstrated. Gateway credits remain the existing service prepayment option and do not substitute for direct seller settlement.

Amounts are devnet test tokens, represented as integer base units and transported as decimal strings; quotes and receipts identify the exact network and mint. Job and financial events must be append-only, with unique operation, receipt and earnings constraints.

One receipt may fund exactly one job and produce one earnings event. Lost replies remain pending and must reconcile the same operation. A paid job that fails remains visibly paid. Refunds are separate seller-funded transfers to an owner-verified address, capped at the settled amount and counted only after finality; automatic refunds and escrow are deferred.

## Private data and honest privacy

The public catalogue must be a sanitized projection. Private jobs, inputs, receipts and files are available only to their authorized participants. Exposed tables require RLS and explicit grants. Clients cannot directly update quotes, jobs, payments or earnings; trusted transition APIs enforce state and actor checks. Storage buckets remain private, with short-lived signed download links. Service keys stay server-side.

The marketplace operator, seller, facilitator and model provider can see the buyer–seller relationship and plaintext job data they process. The pool targets only the explicit on-chain deposit-to-payment link. Amounts, fresh payment wallets and timing remain public; no metadata anonymity or anonymity score is promised. See [privacy](./privacy.md).

Hosted execution needs isolation and controlled network access without wallet secrets. The current local Node runner does not establish a hosted seller sandbox. Listing text, tool responses and result files are untrusted; they cannot expand permissions or execute scripts in the app origin.

## Required defaults and deferred scope

| Limit | v3.2 default |
|---|---|
| Active execution / tool calls | 10 minutes / 8 calls |
| Execution attempts | One attempt; retries cannot silently repeat payment or provider cost |
| Quote TTL | 5 minutes |
| Worker lease / heartbeat | 60 seconds / 15 seconds |
| Attachments | At most 10, each at most 20 MiB |
| Content retention | 30 days |
| Paid delegation depth | One specialist per hire; no paid recursive delegation |

These are marketplace requirements, not changes to the existing gateway's 600-second quote default or other local configuration. Deployment, enforcement, cleanup and timeout evidence remain outstanding.

Auctions, reputation, escrow, automatic refunds, arbitrary uploaded code/open code hosting, multi-seller bundles and nonzero fees are deferred. Read-only connector access is the default; external publishing is not authorized by a hire.

Before implementation or release, complete the [discovery, delivery and acceptance gates](./marketplace-triage.md). No pool-contract change is required solely for this marketplace extension.

# Marketplace implementation triage

**Assessment date: 17 October 2026.** This is documentation and source inspection, not a marketplace test run. No marketplace acceptance case has passed in this checkout. The required product scope is [PRD v3.2 §26](./marketplace.md); the triage retains all of it.

## Scope and source snapshot

The docs branch previously contained PRD v3.1. It now contains the byte-identical v3.2 amendment read from the main checkout, including §26 and backlog T17–T23. Spec SHA-256: `d4b4170e9880dc70654f1916a99a0cb36c2d4f66ab69b83c30fcca1a39b20d72`. The amendment was uncommitted in the main checkout when inspected; synchronizing this copy does not claim that another branch has been merged.

Implementation findings below refer to docs-branch source `8bfe4a2` (application baseline `fe13778`). The concurrent marketplace branch has a Phase 0 inventory and a draft limits module; those working files are not merged here and are not evidence of deployed identity, jobs or payments. The Phase 0 inventory's older proposals to make Supabase optional for the marketplace or defer managed templates do not override the accepted v3.2 scope. Supabase is required for the marketplace; it remains unnecessary for local T00–T16 operation.

## Reusable foundation and concrete gaps

| Area | Inspected source | Finding / required next work |
|---|---|---|
| Local authority | `services/control/src/http/actor.ts`, `auth/session.ts`, `ledger/authorize.ts` | Local wallet challenge, agent-scoped credentials and atomic reservations exist. Add a separate cloud identity and authenticated outbound connection without replacing local spending authority. |
| Agents and queue | `packages/db/migrations/control/0001_ledger.sql`, `services/runner/src/roles/` | Agent roles and job kinds are fixed; no generic specialist runtime or participant job board. T19 must generalize templates, leases, input requests and validated artifacts. |
| Service binding | `packages/x402-client/src/binding.ts`, control `approved_service` schema | Existing binding checks origin, network, mint, seller `payTo`, derived ATA, amount and allowed fee payer. This is reusable code, not a verified marketplace hire or arbitrary live seller support. |
| Managed merchant | `services/gateway/src/gateway.ts`, `purchases.ts` | Gateway uses one configured merchant. Block managed paid listings until per-listing recipient/version binding and direct settlement tests pass; never route seller payments through the operator. |
| Free execution | Control `service_sku` constraints and gateway API schemas | Existing purchase paths require positive USDC or credit usage. Define an explicit free quote/execution path; do not fake a settled payment or charge a nominal token to bypass this gap. |
| Cloud data / files | Workspace manifests and migrations | No Supabase client, marketplace schema/RLS, private Storage policy or transition API in this checkout. Tenant isolation and signed downloads are untested. |
| Results / earnings / refunds | Gateway purchase/result cache and control content artifacts | Existing local results and financial events are reusable; marketplace participant access, receipt-to-job/earnings uniqueness and seller-funded capped refunds are missing. |
| Hosted runtime / connectors | `services/runner/src/safe-fetch.ts`, restricted role tools | Local origin/tool checks exist. No hosted sandbox, credential broker, reviewed remote-seller callback authentication or grant-revocation flow is demonstrated. |

## T17 contract discovery is incomplete

The inventory can identify existing contracts; it cannot declare marketplace schemas frozen yet:

| Contract | Existing authoritative shape | Missing marketplace decision / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Quote | `packages/contracts/src/gateway/api.ts`: operation, SKU, request digest; `QuoteView` adds account, recipient binding, charge, gateway, expiry and purchase state | Freeze listing/runtime/payout versions, participants, scope/input digest, explicit free or paid mode and zero-fee fields. Bind these to the local operation before any authority release. |
| Payment | `packages/contracts/src/control/states.ts`: authorization, funding, merchant, fulfilment and recovery are distinct; transition triggers and outbox/inbox already exist | Freeze cloud request/acknowledgement, expiry/replay/revocation rules and finalized receipt identity. A cloud projection cannot create local reservations or mark a payment settled. |
| Result | `services/gateway/src/purchases.ts`: authenticated cached result or explicit failure/uncertainty; local content artifact APIs | Freeze participant access, artifact validation, attempt/lease identity, late-result rejection and paid-but-failed handling. Define one receipt → one job → one earnings event. |

T17 requires the repository/commit, entry points, schemas/state machines, program/circuit/artifact identity, proof/recovery evidence, x402/facilitator/recipient rules, wallet boundary, auth, queue and deployment inventory. The existing M2 and local integration manifests supply a baseline; they do not verify marketplace behavior. No marketplace migration or pool-contract change should precede completion of this discovery gate. This documentation pass does not perform those changes.

## Delivery gates T17–T23

| Task | Dependencies | Current triage | Completion evidence required |
|---|---|---|---|
| T17 Discovery | T00–T08 | **In progress outside this checkout; not complete here.** Inventory exists, marketplace schemas are not frozen here. | Versioned inventory, agreed quote/payment/result schemas and explicit gaps before migration or contract work. |
| T18 Identity and protected data | T17 | **Not implemented here; not yet run.** | Supabase wallet sign-in, reviewed catalogue/seller setup, workspaces, grants/RLS and private Storage; anonymous, buyer A/B, seller and worker isolation tests. |
| T19 Generic agents and free jobs | T17–T18, T11–T13 | **Not implemented here; not yet run.** Fixed local roles are reusable foundations. | Template-driven agents; free job input, lease, result/download flow; duplicate/crash delivery leaves one current result. |
| T20 Direct paid hiring | T09, T19 | **Blocked** on marketplace contracts, verified recipients and receipt binding. | One finalized direct seller payment funds one job and one earnings event; explicit zero fee; ambiguous outcomes block replacement payments. |
| T21 Discovery and automation | T20 | **Not implemented here; not yet run.** | Search/propose, owner approval for new sellers, schedule dedupe and revoke; malicious listings cannot alter recipient, permissions or service approval. |
| T22 Connectors and remote sellers | T21 | **Not implemented here; not yet run.** | Reviewed MCP/API adapters, credential broker, authenticated callbacks, least-privilege/revoked-grant tests; a new seller earns from a genuine devnet job. |
| T23 Recovery and release | T22 | **Not implemented here; not yet run.** | Finalized capped seller refunds, uncertain settlement, offline/stale-worker behavior, restore/suspension and every §26.6 check below. |

Priority is to finish T17 before T18 changes, then follow the stated dependency graph. The remaining T11–T15 live-inference evidence is still required; marketplace documentation or a free mock job does not complete it.

## Acceptance matrix — all 14 §26.6 checks

Every row below is **not yet run for the marketplace**. Existing local/P0 tests are supporting foundations only.

| ID | Required check | Evidence needed to close it |
|---|---|---|
| MKT-01 | Connected but unsigned wallet cannot read private records | No authenticated cloud session: API/database/Storage deny private reads. |
| MKT-02 | Buyer A cannot read buyer B's data | Cross-tenant tests against transition APIs, direct exposed-table access and private Storage. |
| MKT-03 | Seller sees assigned jobs only and cannot mutate price, recipient, participants or payment | Seller role negative read/write tests and unchanged immutable quote/payment fields. |
| MKT-04 | Wallet switching cannot transfer ownership | Switch wallet/session; old workspace/job/file access is denied and ownership stays unchanged. |
| MKT-05 | Changed recipient/mint/network/amount, expired quote or unapproved seller rejected locally | Tamper each bound field and replay expiry/approval cases; no proof or merchant signature released. |
| MKT-06 | Concurrent hires stay within all budgets | Competing hires for final allowance; local reservations admit only fitting exposure. |
| MKT-07 | One receipt funds one job and one earnings event | Replay receipt across jobs/accounts and concurrently; unique finalized mapping persists after restart. |
| MKT-08 | Lost withdrawal/settlement replies and post-settlement worker crash do not duplicate payment | Kill/drop-response tests at cloud/local/seller boundaries, same operation reconciled, one settlement. |
| MKT-09 | Settled-but-failed jobs remain visibly paid | Seller/provider failure after finality; receipt retained, job failure shown separately from payment. |
| MKT-10 | Refunds never exceed settled payment | Cumulative/duplicate refund tests, owner-verified destination and finalized transfers only. |
| MKT-11 | Stale lease cannot complete a job | Expire/reassign lease, submit late result; old worker rejected, one current result retained. |
| MKT-12 | Malicious result files cannot run scripts in app origin | Hostile HTML/SVG/file tests for preview, downloads and MIME/disposition handling. |
| MKT-13 | Offline controller means no new spending | Disconnect local controller; no cloud action can release a proof/signature or bypass the paused state. |
| MKT-14 | No pool-contract change solely for marketplace | Program/circuit/manifest comparison and regression checks show reused private funding invariants. |

For each row attach the tested commit/environment, actors, exact scenario, expected/observed result, failures/skips and redacted artifacts. Attach actual devnet seller settlement/earnings evidence for paid acceptance; fixtures and local signatures cannot fill it. These documentation IDs label requirements; they are not implemented test names.

## External setup and remaining decisions

A selected/configured Supabase project, reviewed seller endpoints/identities, operator-funded inference where used, devnet RPC/facilitator availability and test-token/SOL sponsorship are external dependencies. Supabase adoption and marketplace inclusion are already owner decisions, not open scope questions. Deployment/provider credentials, hosted runtime isolation technology, exact frozen schemas and the operator publication/review process still need implementation choices and evidence. No runnable marketplace environment-variable contract is defined here; do not invent one or publish service keys.

Supabase's official [Web3 sign-in](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-web3), [RLS](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security) and [Storage access-control](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage/security/access-control) documentation informs the planned boundary. Those product capabilities do not demonstrate Veilo's implementation. Keep service keys server-side; an authenticated session alone does not prove tenant isolation or local spending approval.

# Eight-step demo and evidence checklist

**Status:** complete integrated devnet acceptance evidence is missing here. The parallel deployment branch records an earlier gateway execution, but its run state, ledger, live inference receipts and task artifacts are absent here; recover/review them before paying again. Local rehearsal is **verified on local test validator** with a **fixture / mock provider**. M2 has its separate devnet proof/Echo record. Do not fill missing agent evidence with local signatures or Echo transactions.

This eight-step script covers the original T00–T16 workspace. The v3.2 marketplace has separate [T17–T23 gates and acceptance checks](./marketplace-triage.md); completing this script does not demonstrate seller hiring, Supabase isolation or marketplace earnings/refunds.

## Prepare once

Follow [running Veilo](./running.md) and [deployment](../deployment.md), including manifest-compatible proof files. Configure the funded demo owner (`FUNDING_KEY_PATH`), sponsor, approval authority, gateway merchant/ATA and devnet facilitator; configure the operator-funded provider and ceiling locally. No secret belongs in evidence.

```sh
pnpm demo:run
# When readiness passes, run all steps below in one resumable execution:
pnpm demo:run -- --execute --confirm
# After completion:
pnpm evidence:export
```

`demo:run` starts isolated backend services on ports 4701–4705, with dashboard Origin `http://localhost:4700`; it does not launch a dashboard. Run state is `work/demo/devnet-state.json`. Preserve it and rerun the same execute command after interruption; do not delete it to force a retry. The script activates seeded policies, changes Mira's limit, revokes Prince and exits change: review this plan before execution.

For UI recording, connect a dashboard to the same run's service ports, owner and Origin. The generated non-provider configuration is `work/demo/devnet/<runId>/demo.env`; launch the dashboard from the repository root with `VEILO_ENV_FILE=work/demo/devnet/<runId>/demo.env pnpm --filter @veilo/dashboard dev` (POSIX shell; set the environment variable separately in PowerShell). The backend processes stop when the script completes; later screenshots require restarting those same databases/credentials. Do not record an empty default workspace as if it were the funded run. Browser extension signing is still **not yet run**; the script signs with owner-local key files.

Evidence root: `artifacts/evidence/demo-<runId>/` (currently absent). In the steps below, names such as `steps.b-shawn-topup` identify JSON keys, not additional commands. Every **TODO** is intentionally unfilled until the operator run and evidence review.

## 1. Show network, pool, membership and policies

**Action:** read-only `pnpm demo:run`; during execution inspect `0-policies` and `a-deposits`. Show the dashboard network/privacy views and three policy cards if connected to this run. Three deposits in the integrated demo belong to one owner; M2's two participants were synthetic. Neither is a measured anonymity set.

**Expected evidence:** deployment/circuit manifests, `summary.json` network/program/pool, `steps.0-policies`, deposits and approvals; public amounts and small-set warning.

**TODO — demo deployment/approval/deposit transaction hashes:** pending recovered-run evidence or a newly accepted operator run. **TODO — screenshot 01:** network, pool limitations and three active policies.

## 2. Show Shawn below threshold and check now

**Action:** `b-shawn-topup` reads zero usable credits (<200,000), resumes Shawn and calls authenticated `POST /agents/:id/run`; the dashboard equivalent is Shawn's “Check now.” The scheduled and manual checks use the same deterministic logic.

**Expected evidence:** `summary.json` → `steps.b-shawn-topup.creditsBefore`, plus purchase/episode state and the post-check balance. The script records the manual invocation; do not call that alone proof of an unattended scheduled execution.

**TODO — screenshot 02:** low balance and the check/episode. **TODO — unattended scheduler evidence:** record a scheduler-triggered top-up separately if submission claims genuine autonomous execution.

## 3. Show proof funding, x402 and one issuance

**Action:** wait for `b-shawn-topup` to deliver the credit pack. Show the purchase's funding and merchant legs, fresh payer and exactly one 1,000,000-unit issuance. The merchant here must be the Veilo gateway; PayAI is the facilitator. M2 used Echo instead.

**Expected evidence:** `steps.b-shawn-topup.purchase`, `ledger.json` purchase `chainAttempts`/states and credits before/after; deployment/key hashes in the export.

**TODO — Shawn withdrawal and gateway settlement hashes:** pending recovered-run evidence or a newly accepted operator run. **TODO — screenshot 03:** purchase drawer and one issuance.

## 4. Run Prince research

**Action:** `c-prince-research` submits the task to the runner. Inspect the approved fixed-price research choice, prepaid `analyze` usage (or explicitly recorded permitted per-call fallback) and saved cited brief.

**Expected evidence:** task/purchases in `ledger.json`, `steps.c-prince-research`, `inference-receipts.json`, and `artifacts/research_brief-*.md`. Sources remain fictional CC0 demo fixture data even when inference is live. Provider receipts must say live/operator-funded; fixture output cannot meet this gate.

**TODO — Prince withdrawal/merchant hashes and live inference receipt:** pending recovered-run evidence or a newly accepted operator run. **TODO — screenshot 04:** approved service, categorized usage and attributable brief.

## 5. Approve handoff and run Mira

**Action:** `d-handoff-mira` approves `POST /handoffs/:id/decision` then starts Mira. Dashboard equivalents are handoff approval and the campaign form. Inspect the **direct private x402** `content-package` purchase, three editable drafts and seven-day calendar. No social publishing is authorized.

**Expected evidence:** `steps.d-handoff-mira`, direct payment in `ledger.json`, live receipt, `artifacts/content_draft-*.md` and `artifacts/content_calendar-*.json`. Distinguish direct USDC spend, credits consumed and sponsored planning costs.

**TODO — Mira withdrawal/merchant hashes and live inference receipt:** pending recovered-run evidence or a newly accepted operator run. **TODO — screenshot 05:** approved handoff, direct purchase, drafts and calendar.

## 6. Repeat a logical purchase

**Action:** `e-duplicate-check` repeats Prince's stable research intent and Shawn's check. Inspect the same purchase ID and zero new purchases; confirm neither settlement nor service execution duplicated. A skipped research repeat is a failed recording gate, not a pass.

**Expected evidence:** `steps.e-duplicate-check` (`samePurchase`, `newPurchases`), unchanged chain-attempt/payment/issuance counts. Local IDEM-01/X402-03/04 fault tests support deeper replay behavior; they remain local evidence.

**TODO — duplicate outcome / no-new-payment comparison:** pending recovered-run evidence or a newly accepted operator run. **TODO — screenshot 06:** same operation/result and unchanged counters. No new signature is expected.

## 7. Reject concurrent over-budget requests and revoke independently

**Action:** `f-over-budget-and-revoke` lowers Mira's remaining allowance below a package, sends two concurrent requests and requires both rejected. It revokes Prince and attempts another worker tool call. This differs from the local CAP-02 final-allowance race, which tests that only fitting exposure is admitted.

**Expected evidence:** `steps.f-over-budget-and-revoke.overBudget`, revoke result and `afterRevoke`; no additional released authority. Pause/revoke cannot cancel a proof/signature already released; show live exposure if present.

**TODO — concurrent rejection / revoked-worker response:** pending recovered-run evidence or a newly accepted operator run. **TODO — screenshot 07:** independent agent stop and limits. No payment signature is expected for denied work.

## 8. Owner exit and recovery, with privacy warning

**Action:** `g-owner-exit` prepares, signs/registers and finalizes a public exit of the largest spendable change note to the owner. Show the warning before signing. Public exit may reveal label/value and aggregate spending by subtraction.

**Expected evidence:** `steps.g-owner-exit`, `summary.json.exit` and the owner's resulting public balance. It exits one change note, not every remaining note, and does not demonstrate funded-wallet recovery.

**TODO — integrated owner-exit hash:** pending recovered-run evidence or a newly accepted operator run. **TODO — screenshot 08:** warning, finalized exit and remaining funds.

For a separate funded-wallet recovery demonstration, use the dashboard Recovery Center only after the existing merchant authority is settled or proven expired, prepare/confirm recovery to the configured owner destination and record its outcome. `demo:run` does not create this scenario. Local REC-03/REV-01/BAK-01 supply existing recovery evidence; M2 records original/change public exits separately.

**TODO — funded-wallet recovery hash and screenshot 09:** separate operator scenario, if claimed. Never fabricate a recovery to fill this field.

## Freeze and review

Export with `pnpm evidence:export`. Retain the exact source commit, lockfile hashes, circuit/setup manifest, UTC execution time and reviewer. Inspect `summary.json`, `ledger.json`, `inference-receipts.json`, useful output artifacts, negative outcomes and screenshots together. The exporter supplies artifact hashes but does not currently attach a source Git commit; add it to the submission record.

The exporter currently adds devnet explorer URLs to every signature it finds, including local integration records. Use each source file's environment to classify it; local signatures do not become devnet evidence. See [handoff gaps](../handoff.md). Secret scanning is useful but does not review private prompts or screenshot contents. Keep notes, witnesses, key files, credentials, decryption roots and encrypted backups owner-local.

# Source provenance and license map

Reviewed 17 October 2026 against source snapshot `fe13778`, PRD Part VI and the exact published dependency archives noted below. Root `NOTICE` retains the complete zx402 MIT notice; it does not license all of Veilo. **Owner decision: select Veilo's own license.** No root `LICENSE` has been added.

## Architecture and adapted invariants

[zx402](https://github.com/Marcussy34/zx402/tree/9da88d099bb1ad28c0de3e2b0b7e15e2a1fd198d), by Marcus Tan, is the architectural reference pinned by PRD sections 18/23 and Part VI. That local corpus includes its MIT license, copyright 2026 Marcus Tan. Its pooled-note/spend/insert/public-exit flow, private change, fresh-payer x402 and privacy/trust explanations inform Veilo's circuits, privacy SDK, wallet/relayer and guides. The adaptation changes Cardano/BLS12 to Solana accounts/BN254 and adds delegated policies, shared credits and durable multi-agent workflows.

The source map is PRD section 23: `circuits/src/{spend,insert,ragequit}.circom`, `packages/crypto`, `packages/sdk/src/{sdk,x402}.ts` and the reference privacy/payment/trust guides. Veilo's counterparts are `circuits/src/{spend,insert,exit}.circom`, `packages/privacy-sdk`, `packages/x402-client`, `services/{wallet,relayer}` and the public guides. This is a reference/adaptation map, not proof of which lines were copied. The companion upstream archive was not present in this worktree; the MIT notice was checked against the embedded corpus. Retain notices if additional reused files are identified.

Privacy Pools is acknowledged as architectural lineage; this checkout does not identify directly vendored Privacy Pools contracts. zx402's Cardano transactions and performance claims must never be presented as Veilo Solana evidence.

# Veilo documentation

An owner-controlled workspace for AI agents that buy approved resources within delegated budgets, using a shared private funding pool on Solana devnet. PRD v3.2 extends it with a marketplace of reviewed, paid specialist agents.

## Current verification status

The recorded M2 pool/Echo smoke is **verified on devnet**. Integrated payments/recovery are **verified on local test validator**; Shawn, Prince and Mira use a **fixture / mock provider** in local rehearsal. A parallel branch reports a later devnet gateway execution, but complete task/live-inference acceptance evidence is missing here. Marketplace acceptance is **not yet run** in this checkout. See [current status](./guide/status.md), [running Veilo](./guide/running.md), the [demo checklist](./guide/demo.md) and [handoff gaps](./handoff.md). The setup is deterministic and for development test funds only; this is not an audited or mainnet-ready system.

## Marketplace scope in v3.2

Buyers will discover reviewed specialist agents, hire one at a fixed price and receive deliverables through a private job board. Sellers will complete operator-reviewed setup and receive payment directly through x402, with an explicit zero platform fee and earnings shown as finalized receipt history. Supabase holds marketplace identity and product data; local control and wallet services retain spending authority. These marketplace features are accepted requirements, not implemented capabilities in this checkout.

See [Marketplace](./guide/marketplace.md) for buyer/seller flows, two sign-ins, direct settlement and limits, and [implementation triage](./guide/marketplace-triage.md) for every T17–T23 gate and §26.6 acceptance check. The existing local workspace continues to run without Supabase.

## Existing local workspace

Create agents that can buy approved digital resources and complete jobs within your rules. Give each agent a name, objective, trigger, budget and service permissions. The workspace combines useful agent work, independent spending controls and a private funding path.

### User flow

1. Connect your owner wallet and deposit test funds into the shared pool.
2. Create an agent and configure its job, allowed services, budget and approval mode.
3. Start a task or enable its trigger. The agent proposes the resources it needs.
4. The control and wallet services check policy, reserve funds and authorize a permitted purchase.
5. A proof-authorized pool withdrawal funds a fresh payment wallet, which pays the service through x402.
6. Receive the result and inspect spending, outputs and pending operations. Pause or revoke an agent when needed.

### Why combine these pieces?

- **Delegation:** agents can purchase the resources their jobs need without repeated manual payments when policy permits.
- **Control:** separate agent limits and shared workspace caps constrain financial exposure.
- **Funding privacy:** the payment path aims to remove the explicit link from a particular deposited note to its payout.
- **Owner visibility:** keep local attribution of which agent requested a purchase and what it produced.
- **Recovery:** track uncertain payments and delivery separately so retries do not blindly create another charge.

Veilo's contribution is the integration of owner-created agents, delegated policy, private funding and useful paid workflows. Privacy pools and x402 are existing foundations; the design does not claim to invent them.

### Does a private payment hide which agent or wallet paid?

The merchant payment wallet and transfer are public. The intended privacy property is hiding the explicit link back to the original deposited note and its funding wallet. Public transactions do not carry a stable agent name or workspace ID, but this does not make the agent unidentifiable to everyone: the owner retains local attribution, the gateway can link authenticated usage, and timing or amounts can support correlation. See [privacy and trust](./guide/privacy.md).

## Follow the system

1. [Architecture](./guide/architecture.md): components, trust boundaries and enforcement ownership.
2. [Payment lifecycle](./guide/payments.md): private funding, ordinary x402 and durable recovery.
3. [Privacy and trust](./guide/privacy.md): intended protection, public metadata and operator visibility.
4. [Security model](./security/assessment.md): permission tiers, authentication and enforcement boundaries.
5. [Verification requirements](./security/evidence.md): acceptance cases the implementation must demonstrate.

## Create your own agents

The existing workspace lets owners create and configure named agents using credit-manager, research and content role templates. Shawn, Prince and Mira are seeded examples. PRD v3.2 requires generic agents and specialists with owner-defined instructions/tools; that execution model is pending T19. All agents remain subject to workspace-wide limits.

### Demo examples

| Agent | Job | Intended purchased outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Shawn | Monitor the shared gateway credit balance | Buy one bounded inference-credit pack when the threshold is crossed |
| Prince | Research an owner-supplied question | Buy approved data/inference and save an attributable research brief |
| Mira | Create content from a brief or approved research handoff | Directly buy a content package and save three editable posts plus a seven-day calendar |

The model proposes work. An independent wallet/control service authorizes money. Agents share the workspace treasury and gateway credit account, with separate agent limits.

## Network and service boundaries

- Settlement uses test assets on Solana devnet. SOL pays chain costs separately.
- Real inference is paid for by the gateway operator's OpenRouter account. Test USDC does not replenish commercial provider funds.
- Gateway credits are application service entitlements, not OpenRouter account credits or redeemable money.
- Research fixtures must be labeled demo data; fixture output does not prove live search.
- Content scheduling means planning dates and local editable posts. External social publishing is outside the current scope.

# Agent workflows

**Verification scope:** see [current status](./status.md). The recorded M2 proof run is **verified on devnet**; integrated flows are **verified on local test validator** with a **fixture / mock provider**. Full devnet agent acceptance lacks complete evidence here. Marketplace acceptance is **not yet run** in this checkout.

## Owner-created agents

Creation/configuration is implemented through owner control routes. Execution uses the credit-manager, research and content role templates; it is not an arbitrary agent runtime. New research/content agents also need scoped worker credentials in the runner configuration; `demo:seed` initially provisions the seeded Prince/Mira roles. Natural-language policy drafting is not implemented.

Owners create and configure agents with their own names, jobs, triggers, budgets and service permissions. The examples below demonstrate three useful workflows; they do not limit the agents an owner can create. Each agent operates within its configured tools and services and the workspace's shared financial limits.

One runner uses different role instructions, tools and independently enforced policies. Names are editable display fields, not authority identities. Owner-created agents cannot autonomously create spending subagents or expand their own permissions.

## Marketplace agents and specialists — pending T19–T22

The v3.2 target allows arbitrarily named agents with their own instructions, triggers and tools. Shawn, Prince and Mira become managed templates. A buyer can manually hire one reviewed specialist, or let an agent search and propose within owner-defined permissions; a new seller needs owner approval. That approval cannot bypass budgets or change an immutable payout recipient.

The current runner and database still restrict execution to three coded roles; free specialist jobs, searchable seller listings, reviewed managed/remote execution and connector grants are not implemented here. Read-only connectors are the default; arbitrary uploaded code and paid recursive delegation are excluded. The existing local Prince-to-Mira handoff is not marketplace hiring. See [marketplace](./marketplace.md) and [T17–T23 triage](./marketplace-triage.md).

## Shawn — shared-credit replenishment

The threshold decision is deterministic and requires no paid model call. Default check interval: 60 seconds. Demo policy: threshold 200,000 gateway units, pack 1,000,000 units, at most 1.00 test-USDC per pack, 3.00 test-USDC rolling 24-hour cap, 10-minute minimum interval between successful top-ups, one unresolved top-up per shared account.

Read a fresh balance/version. If low and allowed, create one stable purchase operation. Repeated checks reuse it. Wait for settlement and credited-once issuance before evaluating another purchase. Stale balances or unresolved outcomes pause the check. A manual “Check now” must execute the same logic as the scheduler.

## Prince — paid research

The owner supplies the question, optional sources and deadline. Prince proposes a plan, chooses at least one relevant approved fixed-price data service and purchases permitted inference through credits or a separate direct payment. Save a brief with evidence links and purchase references. Label licensed fixture data explicitly and mark unsupported claims; do not fabricate citations.

## Mira — content creation

The owner supplies topic, audience, channels, voice and deliverables, or explicitly approves a Prince handoff. Mira chooses an approved content SKU and, in this example workflow, pays directly through the private devnet x402 path. The local rehearsal uses a **fixture / mock provider** to produce three editable channel-specific posts and a seven-day calendar. Operator-funded live inference with the direct devnet content payment is **not yet run**.

Track editable, needs review, approved for export and archived. Editing, approving or changing a planning date does not buy inference. Regeneration is a new budgeted operation. The current scope has no social credentials or publishing tool.

## Bounded execution

Default limits per task: eight tool calls, three paid purchases and ten minutes. Sponsored planning permits at most two bounded calls with a fixed allowlisted model; report this cost separately. Execution must remain within the configured owner policy.

A model refusal is not a financial control. Malicious retrieved text remains untrusted, and the independent policy/signing boundary must reject unauthorized requests even if the model follows that text.

# Architecture

**Verification scope:** see [current status](./status.md). The recorded M2 proof run is **verified on devnet**; integrated flows are **verified on local test validator** with a **fixture / mock provider**. Full devnet agent acceptance lacks complete evidence here. Marketplace acceptance is **not yet run** in this checkout.

Veilo separates agent planning, financial authority, public-chain enforcement and paid-service delivery. The implemented owner stack is local, with one owner per workspace and distinct processes, credentials and secret access. The accepted v3.2 marketplace adds multiple independent buyer/seller accounts and cloud product records; it does not make a workspace multi-owner. These are application/process credential boundaries on a trusted owner host, not an OS sandbox against a compromised process. Owners can create and configure agents; demo agents are examples of roles running within the same authority boundaries.

## The architecture in plain language

The owner defines the job and spending rules. The **agent runner** decides what resources would help. The **control service** checks limits and reserves the budget. The **wallet service** holds private notes, generates proofs and signs only allowed payments. The **pool program** verifies the withdrawal on chain. A fresh wallet then makes a normal **x402** payment, and the **gateway** delivers the purchased service.

This separates decision-making from financial authority: a model proposing a purchase cannot grant itself permission to spend. The owner sees agent-level activity locally, while the public payment path avoids publishing those agent identifiers.

## 1. Agent authorization

[Diagram definition included below.]

## 2. Private funding and public settlement

[Diagram definition included below.]

## 3. Paid service delivery

[Diagram definition included below.]

## Components and authority

| Component | Responsibility | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Owner dashboard | Wallet session, agent configuration, approvals, monitoring | Authenticated UI; never asks for the owner's seed phrase |
| Control service | Policies, scheduler, atomic reservations, audit events, revocation epochs | Single authority for workspace/agent/task spending allowances |
| Agent runner | Bounded planning, catalog selection, requesting purchases, saving outputs | No note database, provider key, arbitrary signer or policy mutation |
| Wallet service | Encrypted notes, local proofs, constrained fresh-wallet signing, recovery | Checks current policy before releasing financial authority |
| Relayer / indexer | Sponsor permitted chain costs, submit withdrawals, rebuild public tree state | Does not receive note secrets; indexer cannot invent accepted roots |
| Privacy pool program | Verify proofs, conserve value, consume nullifiers, enforce bound destinations and owner exits | On-chain enforcement; PDA controls the SPL vault |
| Service gateway | Immutable quotes, settlement reconciliation, durable credits, delivery/result cache | Merchant is the gateway operator; credits stay linked to an authenticated workspace |
| x402 facilitator | Verify and settle standard exact SVM payment | Merchant leg only; distinct from the private-withdrawal relayer |
| OpenRouter / data adapter | Bounded real inference or explicitly labeled research data | Provider availability and commercial funding are operator dependencies |

## Implemented stack and source layout

TypeScript, Next.js dashboard, Express gateway, durable workers, SQLite WAL, Rust/Anchor pool program and Circom/snarkjs BN254 Groth16 proofs. Versions are pinned in lockfiles and proof artifacts in `artifacts/circuits/manifest.json`; see [deployment](../deployment.md).

| Source path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `apps/dashboard/` | Owner UI and same-origin proxy to the control API |
| `services/control/`, `services/runner/` | Policy, reservations, scheduler and restricted workers |
| `services/wallet/`, `services/relayer/` | Private state, signing, proofs and public chain adapters |
| `services/gateway/` | x402 routes, credit ledger and provider adapters |
| `packages/contracts/`, `packages/db/` | Shared schemas, migrations and durable state |
| `packages/privacy-sdk/`, `packages/x402-client/` | Witness/encoding logic and constrained payment adapter |
| `programs/privacy-pool/`, `circuits/` | On-chain program and spend/insert/exit circuits |
| `tests/`, `scripts/`, `artifacts/` | Acceptance tests, operator commands and public artifact manifests |

These paths exist in the source snapshot. Documentation has its own dependency manifest and lockfile under `docs/`. The funded dashboard/browser-wallet flow remains **not yet run**; local UI checks are recorded separately in build status T14.

## Marketplace extension — required, not implemented here

Supabase Auth, Postgres and private Storage will hold marketplace identity, catalogue, jobs, artifact metadata and accounting projections. Local control retains policies/reservations/revocation and local wallet retains secrets/proofs/signing. The cloud never becomes a spending authority. It receives acknowledged state through an outbound, authenticated, digest-bound and expiring connection initiated by local control. Spending pauses while control is offline.

Marketplace Web3 sign-in and the existing local wallet challenge are deliberately separate. The local P0 stack still works without Supabase. Seller settlement must go directly to the reviewed recipient; the existing gateway’s single merchant is a blocker for managed paid listings. No pool-contract change is needed solely for the extension. See the [marketplace boundary diagram](./marketplace.md) and [source-based triage](./marketplace-triage.md).

## Enforcement placement

The chain/proofs enforce ownership, approved-set membership for private spends, value conservation, nullifier uniqueness, withdrawal intent and owner exit. The wallet/control service enforces budgets, merchant selection, revocation and signing policy. The gateway enforces paid delivery, credit issuance/debit, request binding and provider cost limits. The model is not a security authority.

Off-chain spending caps are not proof-enforced caps. Compromise of the owner wallet service can bypass its local policy and expose its notes.

## Durable state

Control owns scoped allowance reservations; the gateway owns issued/reserved/consumed credits. Link operations across these databases with stable operation IDs and durable outbox/inbox events. Do not maintain two independently authoritative copies of the gateway balance.

Keep encrypted notes and signer/provider secrets separate from runner-readable activity. A restart must reconcile released proofs, signed transactions and provider attempts before creating new financial authority. See [payments](./payments.md) and [policy](./policy.md).

# Payment lifecycle

**Verification scope:** see [current status](./status.md). The recorded M2 proof run is **verified on devnet**; integrated flows are **verified on local test validator** with a **fixture / mock provider**. Full devnet agent acceptance lacks complete evidence here. Marketplace acceptance is **not yet run** in this checkout.

The private withdrawal and x402 merchant payment are separate transactions. A fresh payment wallet uses ordinary x402; x402 alone does not hide the source of funds.

[Diagram definition included below.]

## Before a purchase

1. Verify devnet genesis, mint owner/decimals, token program, deployment manifest and compatible proof artifacts. Reject mainnet in demo mode.
2. The owner signs a deposit. Track submitted, finalized, indexed, approved and spendable separately. Pending or unapproved notes are unavailable.
3. Control authenticates the requester, creates a stable operation and request digest, and obtains an immutable gateway quote.
4. In one atomic control transaction, check every allowance scope and reserve input note/exposure. A second agent cannot spend that same note or last available allowance.

## Private funding

The wallet service persists a fresh signer before funding it. A local real proof demonstrates note and approved-label membership, valid nullifier, range-checked value/change and an intent bound to pool/program, devnet, mint, payout account, amount, fees, relayer where applicable and expiry.

The on-chain program verifies this proof, consumes the input nullifier, transfers only the bound amount and queues private change atomically. Change becomes spendable only after authenticated insertion finalizes and the witness is rebuilt. The indexer cannot authorize arbitrary tree roots.

The relayer/sponsor funds permitted account creation and fees under separate limits. Sponsorship must not quietly fall back to the identifiable owner's withdrawal fee payment.

## Merchant payment and delivery

The wallet validates the full x402 V2 exact transaction: network, mint, amount, recipient ATA, transfer authority, fee payer, expiry, compute budgets and allowed instruction layout. Reject unrelated transfers, approvals and delegate changes.

The gateway validates the immutable quote/account/request binding and atomically claims the operation and signature before settlement. After finalized settlement, it records one financial event and either issues a credit pack once or authorizes one bounded service attempt. Paid retries return the existing status/result even after quote expiry.

| Payment option | Financial effect |
|---|---|
| Direct per-call x402 | One test-USDC payment; no prepaid debit |
| Credit-pack purchase | One test-USDC payment attributed to Shawn; one gateway issuance |
| Prepaid inference | Consume shared gateway credits and requesting agent usage allowance; no second USDC charge |

Mira's scripted demo uses a **direct private x402 content-package purchase**; its local-validator rehearsal uses a **fixture / mock provider**. A later devnet gateway run is reported on the deployment branch, but Mira's complete live result/receipt evidence is missing here. Shawn demonstrates shared-credit replenishment; Prince may use the prepaid path.

## Marketplace settlement — required, not implemented here

A marketplace quote must bind the reviewed listing, runtime and payout versions, exact seller recipient, scope, network, mint, amount and expiry. The fresh signer pays that seller directly through x402 V2 exact. Execution waits for independently verified finality unless the quote is explicitly free. Quotes/receipts show a zero platform fee; seller earnings are finalized receipt history, not a platform balance. Gateway credits do not replace direct seller settlement.

The current gateway has one configured merchant. Managed paid listings stay blocked until per-listing recipients and receipt-to-job uniqueness are implemented and verified; do not route seller funds through the operator. One finalized receipt may fund one job and one earnings event. Refunds are separate seller-funded, finalized transfers to an owner-verified destination, cumulatively capped at the settled amount; failed delivery must remain visibly paid. These are [v3.2 requirements](./marketplace.md), not evidence that marketplace settlement/refunds work.

## Recovery and failure handling

| Boundary | Required handling |
|---|---|
| Proof released, withdrawal outcome unknown | Keep exposure reserved; reconcile nullifier/chain state and proof expiry |
| Withdrawal finalized, merchant not signed | Track the funded wallet separately from pool notes; resume only within current policy |
| Merchant signed/submitted, response lost | Query the existing signature; do not automatically create another payment |
| Settlement finalized, issuance interrupted | Reconcile and issue the same pack once |
| Provider request outcome unknown | Record uncertain or paid-without-result; no blind retry without upstream idempotency |
| Agent stopped with a funded wallet | Recover only to the configured owner destination after conflicting authority is resolved |

Quote expiry, transaction last-valid block height and proof `valid_until_slot` are different bounds. Expiring a transaction does not necessarily invalidate a released proof that can be placed in another transaction. Release its reservation only after finalized chain evidence proves the authorization is no longer usable and no spend settled.

A public exit requires note ownership proof and the original refund authority. It must remain possible without approved-set membership; it reveals information and does not restore privacy. Test both original and change notes.

---

# Policy and accounting

**Verification scope:** see [current status](./status.md). The recorded M2 proof run is **verified on devnet**; integrated flows are **verified on local test validator** with a **fixture / mock provider**. Full devnet agent acceptance lacks complete evidence here. Marketplace acceptance is **not yet run** in this checkout.

## Permission tiers

| Tier | Permitted behavior | Still prohibited |
|---|---|---|
| Observe | Plan and explain proposals | Releasing spending proofs/signatures |
| Bounded automatic | Purchase without another approval when every applicable rule passes | Exceeding any cap or allowed service binding |
| Approval required | Request explicit owner approval for designated valid purchases | Using approval to bypass hard limits |
| Stopped | Reconcile existing operations | Releasing new spending authority |

Recovery and owner exit remain available through their separate authenticated paths. Editing policy is a distinct owner action. Structured policy changes create drafts that require owner activation. Natural-language policy drafting is not implemented.

## Marketplace approval and offline control — pending

PRD v3.2 keeps every local limit in force for specialist hires. A cloud identity session or cloud policy record cannot authorize spending: local control must install/acknowledge policy proposals and validate an approved seller plus immutable listing/payout/quote/runtime versions. A changed recipient or unapproved seller must stop locally. Concurrent hires share the same local allowance authority.

The required cloud connection uses authenticated, digest-bound, expiring requests initiated outbound by local control. New automatic spending pauses when control is offline; already released authority remains live exposure. Search/propose tools, schedule dedupe, connector grants and callback/lease checks still need marketplace implementation and negative tests. See [triage](./marketplace-triage.md).

## Authorization algorithm

1. Authenticate the worker's bound workspace/agent, and validate supplied task ownership; do not trust an agent ID supplied in JSON.
2. Resolve the stable operation and immutable request/quote. Changed payload for the same operation conflicts before any payment.
3. Validate service origin, gateway identity, SKU, network, mint, recipient and quote bounds.
4. In a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, recheck limits, status, policy version and note availability; create the unique operation/reservation.
5. Recheck policy and revocation epoch before proof release, withdrawal submission and merchant signing.
6. Reconcile finalized outcomes into durable financial events. Keep unknown outcomes reserved.

All writers use the same control authority/database. Multiple worker databases each checking their own caps cannot enforce a workspace cap.

## Independent limits

Every purchase must pass per-purchase, per-task lifetime, per-agent lifetime and rolling 24-hour, workspace lifetime and rolling 24-hour limits. Sponsor SOL fees and recoverable rent have separate bounds. Gateway usage has both scoped usage allowances and shared available credits.

Use integer amounts and decimal strings across APIs. Never compare financial amounts using floating point.

For each cash scope:

```text
available = limit - applicable settled cost - all active reservations
```

For rolling scopes, count settled costs within the preceding 24 hours **plus every live reservation**, even if it is older. A reservation crossing midnight or a rolling boundary does not release exposure.

For gateway credits:

```text
usable credits = issued - consumed - reserved
```

Cash spent, pool tokens, funded fresh-wallet principal, pending change, sponsor lamports, prepaid credits and provider dollars are different units/states. Never sum them into a single balance.

## Revocation and restoration

Pause/revoke must serialize against financial authority release. Already released proof/transaction material may settle until its bound expires; display that live exposure. Do not promise cancellation after release.

Recovering proven unpaid principal may restore eligible allowance. It does not refund a completed service or paid fees, and an external recovered balance does not create a private pool note. Re-entering the pool requires a new deposit.

Persist original settlement timestamps. A restart must not move old spending into a different window. Link refunds to their original expense; an expired expense cannot offset unrelated new rolling-window spending.

---

# Privacy and trust

**Verification scope:** see [current status](./status.md). The recorded M2 proof run is **verified on devnet**; integrated flows are **verified on local test validator** with a **fixture / mock provider**. Full devnet agent acceptance lacks complete evidence here. Marketplace acceptance is **not yet run** in this checkout.

## Intended protection

A shared note-based pool aims to remove the **explicit mapping from a particular deposited note to a withdrawal**. A local proof authorizes the withdrawal without naming the spent deposit. A fresh wallet then pays the merchant through standard x402, and private change remains in the pool.

This requires real on-chain proof verification and authenticated tree updates. Cosmetic address rotation, a trusted database withdrawal authorizer or an ordinary direct x402 payment does not establish this property.

## Which agent or wallet can someone identify?

| Question | Intended behavior |
|---|---|
| Can a public observer see the wallet that pays the merchant? | Yes. The fresh payment address, merchant, amount and timing remain public. |
| Does the withdrawal explicitly identify its original deposited note? | No, in a correctly implemented proof-based flow. Removing this explicit link is the privacy target. |
| Is an agent name or stable workspace ID published with each payment? | It must not be included in chain memos, proof public fields or withdrawal accounts. |
| Can the owner tell which agent spent money? | Yes. The local workspace keeps purchase attribution and outcomes. |
| Can the gateway link purchases or usage? | Yes. Its authenticated workspace account and request data provide off-chain linkage. |
| Is correlation impossible? | No. Small pools, distinctive amounts, funding trails, timing and network metadata can weaken privacy. |

Funding privacy and owner monitoring serve different audiences: the owner retains accountability while the chain omits an explicit deposit-to-withdrawal mapping. This is not a promise that every payment is anonymous to every observer.

## Visibility matrix

| Observer | Information visible in the intended design |
|---|---|
| Public-chain observer | Deposits, source addresses, payout wallets, amounts, mint, merchant payments, fees, timing, public exits and proof public inputs |
| Owner / local wallet service | Note secrets, local agent/task attribution, spending history, recovery metadata and signer material |
| Gateway operator | Authenticated workspace credit account, purchases, requests/prompts, usage, cached results and connection metadata |
| OpenRouter | Operator account, forwarded prompts and model/request metadata; internal workspace IDs are not forwarded by default |
| Relayer / RPC | Submitted public transactions and relevant connection/timing metadata; relayer should not receive note secrets |
| Approved-set / upgrade administrators | Disclosed powers to update approved membership or deployed program code, according to configuration |

Persistent gateway accounts deliberately link service usage off chain. The protocol does not hide prompts from the provider or establish network-level anonymity.

## Marketplace observer boundary — accepted v3.2 scope

Marketplace identity and job records create additional off-chain linkage. The marketplace operator, sellers, facilitators and model providers can see the buyer–seller relationship and plaintext job content they process. Supabase Web3 identity does not hide a buyer from the cloud operator. Private Storage and RLS restrict application access; they do not establish transaction or metadata anonymity.

Hosted seller execution must receive only permitted job data and no wallet secrets. The required retention default is 30 days, with private participant files and short-lived signed download links; these controls are not implemented or verified here. See [marketplace](./marketplace.md) and [acceptance gaps](./marketplace-triage.md).

## Correlation and anonymity limits

A small pool, one active participant, distinctive amounts, closely timed deposit/withdrawal/payment and common operator funding can make linkage plausible. Synthetic demo participants are not independent users. Approved-set size is membership information, not a measured anonymity score.

A separate fee sponsor reduces one obvious source link, but shared RPC endpoints and sponsor funding trails still permit correlation. Public exits and recovery transactions may reveal aggregate spending through subtraction.

Funding privacy does not guarantee anonymity against every observer. Security depends on correct circuits, proof verification, key handling and operational controls.

## Cryptography and setup trust

The current setup uses a deterministic local development powers-of-tau with public beacons. Its toxic waste is derivable: it is unsuitable for production funds. The development setup and unaudited verifier remain material trust risks even though M2 transactions finalized. See [known risks](../security/risks.md).

The Solana proof design uses BN254 Groth16, matching Poseidon parameters and canonical encodings across TypeScript, Circom and Rust.

The deployment manifest must pin circuit/compiler source, curve, hash parameters, public-input order, encoding/vector version, tree depths, proving/verifying-key hashes and setup provenance. Artifact mismatch stops proof generation. A malicious setup, buggy circuit/verifier or excessive upgrade authority can compromise funds/privacy.

Spend and public exit share one pool-scoped nullifier namespace. Bind withdrawal intent to the deployed program/pool, network, mint, exact destination, value/fees and on-chain expiry. The on-chain program reconstructs the intent; an off-chain annotation is insufficient.

## Operational privacy

- Keep note secrets and decryption/signer keys in the local wallet service, inaccessible to the runner.
- Do not put agent names, workspace IDs or gateway account identifiers in chain memos, withdrawal accounts or proof public fields.
- Minimize operator logs; redact secrets, authorization headers and private prompt content before evidence export.
- Retain enough authenticated purchase/result state to reconcile ambiguous outcomes; disclose retention and clean up only after outstanding operations resolve.
- Back up notes, change secrets, paths/rebuild data, fresh-wallet counters and pending operations with an encrypted snapshot. Wallet and control files are copied separately; quiesce writers for an operator snapshot and retain matching gateway state.

The owner machine remains trusted. Local proof generation does not protect secrets from a compromised host.

## Evidence needed before a privacy claim

Demonstrate a real deployed verifier, valid spend/change and owner exit, rejection of invalid proof/context/replay, public-input inspection for stable identifiers, and multiple clearly labeled test deposits. Include the metadata caveats above alongside that evidence. See [security matrix](../security/evidence.md) and [known risks](../security/risks.md).

---

# Running Veilo

**Verification scope:** M2 is **verified on devnet**. Integrated payments/recovery are **verified on local test validator**, agent inference uses a **fixture / mock provider**, and complete devnet agent acceptance evidence is missing here. Marketplace acceptance is **not yet run** in this checkout. See [current status](./status.md).

## Marketplace setup is a separate, pending track

The commands below start the existing local wallet workspace, not the v3.2 marketplace. T18 will add Supabase Auth/Postgres/private Storage; T19–T23 add generic jobs, direct hiring, discovery, connectors and release checks. Supabase is required for that extension but remains unnecessary for the local T00–T16 stack.

No marketplace migration, environment-variable contract, setup script, cloud connection or deployed project is supplied here. Do not invent Supabase key names or use a cloud session as wallet authorization. Follow [marketplace triage](./marketplace-triage.md) and complete the T17 discovery/schema gate before making those changes.

## Application quickstart

Use Node **>=22.14.0 <23**, **pnpm 10.34.6**, and Docker with a running Linux daemon. Native Rust, Solana, Anchor and circom are provided by the pinned Docker toolchain. Allow time/disk/network for the first image and proof builds.

From the repository root:

```sh
corepack enable pnpm
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm toolchain:build
pnpm setup:local
pnpm check:devnet
```

`setup:local` creates `.env` from `.env.example` if missing and local directories. It creates the wallet encryption root only when `OWNER_SERVICE_SECRET_PATH` is configured; it reports service credential paths but does not generate those credentials. Existing secrets are never replaced. Back up the encryption root separately; never commit it.

Edit `.env` locally using [configuration](../configuration.md): set `VEILO_OWNER_PUBKEY`, deployment manifest/program/pool values and role credential/key **paths**. Configure gateway merchant/ATA and facilitator fee payer consistently with the manifest. Missing bindings remain unbound/NOT_READY. For live inference only, the gateway needs an operator-funded OpenRouter key, allowlisted models and a nonzero bounded `OPERATOR_MAX_REAL_USD_MICRO`; test USDC cannot buy provider dollars.

For a new manual local stack, set `OWNER_SERVICE_SECRET_PATH=secrets/owner-service.secret`, `CONTROL_SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_PATH=secrets/control-service.credential`, `WALLET_SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_PATH=secrets/wallet-service.credential` and `RELAYER_SERVICE_CREDENTIAL_PATH=secrets/relayer-service.credential` in `.env`. Generate those three independent credentials without printing them (the directories already exist after setup):

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import {writeFileSync} from "node:fs"; import {randomBytes} from "node:crypto"; for (const role of ["control", "wallet", "relayer"]) writeFileSync(`secrets/${role}-service.credential`, randomBytes(32).toString("hex")+"\n", {flag:"wx", mode:0o600});'
pnpm setup:local
```

This command is for a fresh stack only and refuses existing files. Restore missing credentials for an existing ledger instead of resetting identities. On Windows restrict these credential files with owner-only ACLs; POSIX `mode` does not enforce a Windows ACL. The isolated `demo:run` creates its own credentials and does not use these manual-stack files.

```sh
pnpm demo:seed
pnpm check
pnpm test
pnpm dev
```

Seed policies start as drafts and seeding never issues credits. Open the dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, connect the configured devnet owner wallet and review/activate workspace and agent policies. Control/runner/wallet/gateway/relayer use ports 4101–4105. Run [deployment instructions](../deployment.md) to provision/fund roles and deploy a pool before attempting private purchases. A clean clone has no funded keys, proving keys, databases or provider credentials.

## Proofs, rehearsal and devnet recording

```sh
pnpm test:circuits
pnpm test:program
pnpm test:integration
pnpm demo:run -- --local-rehearsal
```

The integration suite needs the built program (`target/deploy/privacy_pool.so`) and manifest-compatible proving files (`circuits/build/`). The local rehearsal uses throwaway keys, loopback validator/facilitator and **fixture / mock provider**. It writes under ignored `work/demo-rehearsal/evidence/`; its signatures cannot be checked on a devnet explorer.

The parallel deployment branch records an earlier devnet gateway run whose state and acceptance files are absent here. Recover that run’s original state/ledgers and use the corresponding acceptance-checking script version before deciding another paid run is needed; do not reset operation IDs to manufacture a fresh result. See [handoff](../handoff.md#parallel-branch-evidence).

For a new deployment, follow the [devnet runbook](../deployment.md#devnet-deployment-runbook-t09-m2), including key initialization, program-ID alignment/build and circuit manifest checks. Do not regenerate role or proving keys for an existing deployment. The deterministic development setup is unsuitable for production funds.

```sh
pnpm demo:run
# After readiness passes and operator budgets/policies are reviewed:
pnpm demo:run -- --execute --confirm
pnpm evidence:export
```

The first command is read-only and makes no inference call. Execution signs deposits, withdrawals/merchant payments and exit, and incurs bounded operator provider costs. Rerun the same execute command to resume recorded operations. The eight-step [demo script](./demo.md) gives expected records and screenshot placeholders.

The script starts isolated backend services; funded dashboard screenshots require a separately configured dashboard connected to those same run databases/service ports. A screenshot of another workspace is not evidence of this run.

## Backup and recovery

Quiesce service writers before `pnpm backup` for an operator snapshot: wallet and control files are copied separately. Use the encrypted wallet/control snapshot and keep `OWNER_SERVICE_SECRET_PATH` separately. Stop the wallet and other writers before `pnpm restore -- --file <encrypted-backup> --include-control`; retain the matching gateway ledger and credentials rather than resetting issued credits. Startup reconciliation blocks new authority until pending operations are resolved. See [configuration](../configuration.md) for the exact scope. A public exit/recovery can reveal spending/linkage and cannot cancel already released authority.

## Documentation site

The documentation has its own npm lockfile:

```sh
cd docs
npm ci
npm run dev
# Or build and preview:
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The default base is `/Veilo-agent-wallet/`; open the printed base URL. Use `DOCS_BASE=/ npm run build` for a domain root. The build generates `llms.txt`, its intentional compatibility alias `llms.text`, and `llms-full.txt`.

VitePress 1.6.4 uses a pinned Vite 6.4.4 override and Mermaid 12.2.0. Revalidate the build and browser behavior when changing these dependencies. A successful documentation build does not run application/security tests.
